title: Clock and Harbor
premise: In a Baltic port city on the eve of revolution, Theo Nystrom, daughter of a typeface cutter who raised her as his son to spare her the fate of her mother, has survived five years in her father's print shop by learning which silences keep people safe. When an infant is left at the shop's door with a note instructing them to forget the face, Theo recognizes the handwriting as that of a printer executed for seditious pamphlets — and realizes the child is evidence someone powerful wants erased. As the armistice negotiations stall and soldiers begin confiscating presses, Theo must finish printing a hidden run of testimony naming the men who ordered executions, knowing each sheet could save the child's future or burn the workshop down around them. The book ends with the armistice signed too late to stop the raid: the shop burns, but Theo escapes through the harbor fog with the child, the finished testimony, and her father's punches, choosing at last to be seen.
about_author: Ulyana Nystrom is the pen name of a former letterpress compositor who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century print equipment in Baltic port towns. Her fiction draws on family archives of confiscated pamphlets and the oral histories of printers' families who survived three occupations.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet Letters
chapters.summary: Theo, working late sorting type in her father's print shop, establishes the rhythms of survival: which customers to serve, which questions never to answer. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the ache of competence without identity — she cuts type better than any apprentice but must remain invisible.

chapters.title: A Bundle Against the Door
chapters.summary: At dawn Theo finds an infant wrapped in sailcloth on the step, with a note reading 'forget the face.' She recognizes the hand as Aldis Vemmen's — the printer hanged last spring. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: terror cracking into reluctant tenderness; the silence she mastered suddenly feels like complicity.

chapters.title: What Father Cut Away
chapters.summary: Theo confronts her father, Marek, who insists they take nothing to the authorities. He reveals fragments: Vemmen hid something in the shop before his arrest. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the first fracture between father and child; inheritance revealed as burden, not gift.

chapters.title: The Harbor Registers
chapters.summary: Theo visits the harbor master's office under pretense of a print order and learns ships are being requisitioned; the armistice talks are failing. She notes who watches the docks. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into purpose — the city's clock is running down.

chapters.title: Milk, Ink, and Lies
chapters.summary: Days of concealment: Theo invents a dead cousin's widow to explain the baby to neighbors, while rationing milk against emptying shelves. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: exhaustion braided with fierce attachment; the lie of invisibility now protects someone else.

chapters.title: Vemmen's Last Composition
chapters.summary: Searching the locked back room, Theo finds a forme of type set but never printed — testimony naming officers who ordered the executions of strikers, including Vemmen. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: revelation as ignition; justice exists in lead, waiting for hands brave enough.

chapters.title: The Inspector Calls
chapters.summary: Captain Reval of the gendarmerie inspects the shop, lingering over the press. Marek performs deference; Theo reads Reval's interest in Vemmen's case files as hunger, not duty. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: cold fear; the hunter has entered the house and smiled.

chapters.title: Apprentice of No One
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: five years earlier, Marek cutting Theo's hair, burning her mother's letters, teaching her the trade as 'his son.' POV: Marek. Emotional beat: grief explained but not excused; love expressed as erasure.

chapters.title: Paper Is Rationed Too
chapters.summary: Theo trades a family silver spoon for stock paper through a black-market paperhanger, Lotta, who asks no questions but remembers everything. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the price of survival made literal; every sheet bought with a piece of the past.

chapters.title: Night Shift
chapters.summary: First secret print run begins after midnight; the press noise terrifies Theo until Marek joins her at the treadle without a word. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: reconciliation without apology; father and daughter pulling one lever toward the same truth.

chapters.title: The Child Who Cannot Forget
chapters.summary: The baby falls ill with fever; Theo must visit a midwife, risking exposure. The midwife recognizes Vemmen's features in the child and says nothing — but now knows. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: terror tempered by unexpected solidarity among women who keep silences of their own.

chapters.title: Reval's Offer
chapters.summary: Reval returns, ostensibly about a government almanac order, and offers Marek protection in exchange for 'any materials of the deceased printer.' Marek refuses; Theo watches him lie fluently for the first time. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: vertigo — her father becoming someone new before her eyes.

chapters.title: Distribution
chapters.summary: Lotta connects Theo to dockworkers willing to slip testimony pages into ship manifests bound for neutral ports. One courier is caught. POV: alternating Theo and a dockworker, Joss. Emotional beat: hope shadowed by cost; the network is real and therefore bleedable.

chapters.title: The Arrest of Joss
chapters.summary: Joss is taken; Theo must decide whether to flee or finish the remaining sheets. Marek argues flight; Theo argues completion. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized — survival versus justice, and whether they can be the same act.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Rumor
chapters.summary: Reval spreads word that Joss named a printer. Customers vanish; neighbors stare. Theo prints faster, sleeping two hours a night, the baby strapped to her back above the ink smell. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: feverish resolve; work as prayer, deadline as destiny.

chapters.title: Armistice Rumors
chapters.summary: News arrives that terms may be signed within days — and that amnesty will not cover 'printers' crimes.' The testimony must reach foreign hands before borders close. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: cruel irony; peace arriving as a closing door rather than an opening one.

chapters.title: The Locked Room Opens
chapters.summary: Marek finally shows Theo what else Vemmen hid: the original punches for a forbidden typeface used in the suppressed constitution drafts — their true inheritance. POV: Marek. Emotional beat: full confession; the father gives the daughter not safety but legacy.

chapters.title: Last Impression
chapters.summary: The final sheets are pulled at dawn as gendarmes are spotted two streets away. Theo burns the incriminating forme, keeps one copy of everything, and packs the punches. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: solemn triumph; the work is finished even if the world isn't ready.

chapters.title: Fire
chapters.summary: Reval leads the raid; when he finds only ash and an empty cradle frame, he orders the shop burned anyway as punishment. Marek stays behind to delay them. POV: Theo, watching from the harbor wall. Emotional beat: devastation fused with clarity — some prices are paid so others don't have to be.

chapters.title: Fog on the Water
chapters.summary: Lotta smuggles Theo and the baby aboard a coal barge through harbor fog as the shop glows behind them. Joss's fate remains unknown; Reval's name heads the testimony. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: grief carried forward like ballast; escape without victory.

chapters.title: The Face Remembered
chapters.summary: On the open sea, Theo opens the bundle's second note, which she'd never dared read fully: Vemmen asking that the child be raised 'where names are not crimes.' She speaks her own true name aloud for the first time in five years. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: reclamation; inheritance accepted on her own terms.

chapters.title: Setting New Type
chapters.summary: Epilogue, one year later in a free port: Theo works in a small émigré print shop, the baby toddling between cases, the testimony published abroad under Vemmen's name and hers. A letter arrives from the midwife: Reval has been arrested. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: quiet, earned resolution — justice outside the law arrived anyway, and she was there to set it in type.
